newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CULLINAN CENTURY SAVES SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CULLINAN CENTURY SAVES SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: A brilliant unbeaten century from Daryll Cullinan together with a timely intervention from the weather enabled South Africa to escape with a draw in the final test against India at the Wanderers.
Cullinan smashed 122, his third test century, from 194 balls with 15 fours and a six and put on a crucial 127 runs with Lance Klusener for the eighth wicket.
Klusener's 49 came from 77 balls with five fours and a six, but when he fell, caught at short leg off Anil Kumble, there were still nine overs left.
In fading light India were forced to bowl spin from both ends and Allan Donald managed to keep Cullinan company until the umpires offered South Africa the light with four overs remaining.
But India will be rueing the loss of 26 overs which probably cost them a consolation victory in a series won 2-0 by South Africa.
The home side had collapsed to 76 for five in the morning session when a violent thunderstorm forced the players from the field half an hour before the scheduled lunch interval.
When the umpires decided that the outfield had dried enough for play to resume there were only 45.3 overs left. India got to work immediately, reducing South Africa to 95 for seven.

Shaun Pollock, who top scored with 79 in the first innings, was comprehensively bowled by paceman Javagal Srinath for a fourth ball duck and when Dave Richardson was caught at slip off spinner Anil Kumble for seven South Africa were in deep trouble. But Cullinan and Klusener stayed together long enough to ensure the draw.
South Africa captain Hansie Cronje compared Cullinan's match saving innings with Mike Atherton's 10 hour 185 not out on the same ground last year, which saved the second test for England.
Cronje said: "Daryll's knock was every bit as good as Mike's and I know exactly how Sachin (Tendulkar) must have felt because we were frustrated in the same way against England.
"We had got ourselves into all sorts of trouble and it took a near miraculous partnership to save us."
Tendulkar was delighted with his team's performance.
"It was never going to be easy to get back into the third test after losing the series in Cape Town, but we were on top throughout and deserved to win.

"We had no luck, especially with the weather, and we constantly had to ask the umpires who we could bowl because the light was deteriorating. Srinath bowled with great rhythm and Kumble did the damage again and the whole side did an exceptional job."
Resuming at four for one in their second innings, South Africa lost a wicket without addition when Gary Kirsten was caught at third slip off paceman Venkatesh Prasad.
Cullinan and Adam Bacher took the score to 49 without undue alarm, but Prasad broke the stand with the aid of some good fortune.
Bacher, who was lbw playing no shot in the first innings, tried to leave a short ball, but did not get his gloves out of the way and saw the ball cannon onto his stumps when he had made 23.

The innings went into sharp decline when Cullinan ran out his captain Hansie Cronje for six. In the next over Brian McMillan was snared at short leg off Srinath for two and the biggest cheer of the day came when a huge clap of thunder accompaned the beefy all rounder back to the pavilion.
Two balls later the rain came down and effectively that was the moment which decided the test.

India batsman Rahul Dravid, who top scored in each innings with 148 and 81, won the man of the match award while South African paceman Allan Donald was named man of the series after taking 20 wickets at an average of 15.85 in the three tests.
